Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — Reports August ISM Services PMI data
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sep 15-16 Fed meeting rate hike probability, August payrolls release imminent
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
August ISM Services PMI beat expectations at 55.4 (vs 54.2 forecast), driven by a 3.5-year high in new orders (60.9). Input prices surged to 72.6, supply chains remain stretched partly due to tariffs and a U.S.-Israel-Iran war now in month seven. Fed Chair Warsh signaled further hikes may be needed. Markets price a ~64% chance of a 25bps hike at the Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting, with rates currently at 3.50%-3.75%. Services employment remained weak (47.8), adding downside risk to Friday's payrolls print, with consensus at +56K after July's -23K surprise.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES — Core focus is on US economic activity (services PMI), inflation dynamics, and Fed rate policy.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 85 (strongly oriented toward a near-term hike narrative)
Probability of increase: 64% (directly sourced from CME FedWatch as cited in article)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (holding is the minority scenario implied by the data)
Probability of holding: 36% (residual probability implied by the 64% hike pricing)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (no cut narrative present; inflation and demand data are directionally opposite)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (Distinctly hawkish — above-consensus PMI, 3.5-year high new orders, surging input prices at 72.6, explicit Fed Chair Warsh hike signal, and 64% market-implied hike probability at the next meeting all tilt firmly hawkish. The only softening factor is the weak employment sub-index, which marginally tempers the read.)
